h: A museum with a long and lively history
p: World Museum is one of Liverpool's oldest public treasures. It opened in 1851, built around the natural history collection left to the town by the 13th Earl of Derby, and it has been growing ever since. It suffered badly in the Blitz in 1941, when bombing destroyed much of the building and part of the collection, but it bounced back and is now part of National Museums Liverpool.

How long to allow? Families can easily spend half a day here, especially if you add a planetarium show. If you're short on time, pick two floors that match your interests and save the rest for a return trip. Being free, it's an easy place to come back to.

It's a brilliant rainy-day option for kids of all ages. Little ones love the animals and the bug house, older kids tend to head straight for the mummies and the space displays, and grown-ups can lose themselves in the world cultures galleries. There are lifts between floors, so it works well with pushchairs too.

The building is part of William Brown Street's run of grand Victorian landmarks, so you're spoilt for things to pair with it. Right next door is the Central Library, where the round Picton Reading Room is worth a peek even if you're not a bookworm. A few steps further along is the Walker Art Gallery, and across the road stands St George's Hall, one of the city's great neoclassical buildings, with St John's Gardens tucked behind it. Lime Street station is only a few minutes' walk away, so it's easy to reach by train.
